newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq returns as crude oil supplier to France.
newsitem.headline: Iraq returns as crude oil supplier to France.

text.p: Iraq, returning to world oil markets for the first time since the Gulf war, supplied France with 271,000 tonnes of crude in January to become the country's seventh biggest supplier, official figures showed on Tuesday.
Iraq, once a major Middle East supplier to France behind Saudi Arabia and Iran, began exporting oil in December under a plan to ease sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Its return to the market under United Nations restrictions put it in the middle of a league table of French oil suppliers, just ahead of Gabon and Iran, industry ministry figures showed.
Eighth-place Gabon supplied 263,000 tonnes and Iran 258,000 tonnes, while further up the scale Saudi Arabia lost its ranking as France's number one supplier to come second place to Norway.
The North Sea producer delivered 1.731 million tonnes to France in January while Saudi Arabia shipped 1.66 million tonnes, the ministry said.
Britain delivered 1.281 million tonnes, while imports from Russia jumped sharply to 1.064 million from 410,000 in December.
Total French imports run above seven million tonnes monthly.

French oil companies Elf Aquitaine and Total SA are among the international firms that signed deals to buy Iraqi crude during the six-month U.N. oil-for-food pact, designed to raise up to $2 billion to relieve the suffering of ordinary Iraqis as sanctions continue to bite.
They are also expected to line up lucrative oil development contracts inside Iraq once sanctions are eventually scrapped.
In 1989, the last full year before the embargo went into force, France bought six million tonnes or one fifth of its foreign crude oil from Iraq, industry ministry archives show.
France also emerged as a key food supplier to Iraq under the renewable six-month pact, with major private sales of grain and milk powder.
